subject.title: [Bug]: Origin validation fails for custom URL schemes (tauri://, electron://)

question: Which linked exact custom-scheme origin fix should maintainers advance, and what real-behavior proof bar is required for this Gateway browser-origin authorization change?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible and security-relevant, but two open PRs target the same shared Gateway authorization helper and maintainers need to select or sponsor the canonical path before this issue can close.

options.title: Advance one exact-origin PR
options.body: Pick the cleaner current-main candidate, require or explicitly waive real Gateway or desktop-wrapper proof for the auth boundary, and close sibling attempts after merge.

options.title: Pause for broader origin policy
options.body: Defer this exact custom-scheme bug until maintainers decide the broader wildcard or loopback-pattern policy, leaving affected users on the wildcard workaround longer.

options.title: Reject custom-scheme exact allowlisting
options.body: Document wildcard or native-hosting alternatives instead, accepting the security and usability tradeoff for desktop wrappers.

recommendation.title: Advance one exact-origin PR
recommendation.body: Pick the cleaner current-main candidate, require or explicitly waive real Gateway or desktop-wrapper proof for the auth boundary, and close sibling attempts after merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the Gateway origin-check surface and is the strongest history-backed routing candidate for this security-boundary decision.
